item.title: Swapon: Truth, objectivity cornerstones of responsible journalism
item.description:
Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapon on Sunday said truth-seeking and objectivity are the cornerstones of responsible journalism, stressing that public service can only be achieved through rigorous fact-checking and impartial reporting.
Speaking as the chief guest at a seminar marking the 64th founding anniversary of the Department of Mass Communication and Journalism at the University of Dhaka, he said journalism risks losing its credibility when the pursuit of truth is influenced by preconceived positions or ideological bias.
"Journalists must place the pursuit of truth above all else and ensure the accuracy and objectivity of the information they present," he said.
The seminar, titled "The Interconnection of Politics, Power and Journalism: Theory, Reality and the Future," was held at the Professor Muzaffar Ahmed Chowdhury Auditorium of the university's Faculty of Social Sciences, according to Information Ministry Public Relations Officer Imranul Hasan. New Age Editor Nurul Kabir delivered the keynote address.
Swapon said the challenge today is no longer a lack of information but an overwhelming flood of content, where misinformation, disinformation and deliberate manipulation have emerged as serious threats to democracy, governance and society.
"In this environment, journalism's foremost responsibility is to verify facts, uncover the truth and present it to the public with objectivity," he said.
Describing journalism as more than a profession of reporting facts, the minister said it is one of the strongest pillars of public accountability, adding that no democratic state can be strengthened without a free, responsible and independent media.
He also underscored the need to ensure journalists' professional security, economic dignity and an enabling environment for independent reporting, while calling for greater professional capacity to counter misinformation.
During the question-and-answer session, Swapon said defining the limits of freedom of expression is inherently complex, as people express opinions from diverse political, philosophical and ideological perspectives.
However, he stressed that freedom must always be exercised with responsibility.
The minister said the government has initiated efforts to establish a Media Commission aimed at maintaining a balance between power, freedom and accountability.
"We want to establish a participatory and balanced Media Commission through consultations with all stakeholders to ensure harmony among power, freedom and responsibility," he said.
Earlier, Swapon reminisced about his student days at the University of Dhaka, describing his time on campus as one of the most cherished periods of his life and saying that returning to the university evoked a deep sense of nostalgia.
The seminar was chaired by Professor Kazi Mohammad Mahbubur Rahman, chairman of the Department of Mass Communication and Journalism, and moderated by Professor Robayet Ferdous.
University of Dhaka Vice-Chancellor Professor A B M Obaidul Islam attended as the special guest.

item.title: Home Ministe: Govt to build police force free from political influence
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Sunday said the police must not serve as an instrument of any political party or group but should instead become a true friend of people and a symbol of public security.
The government's priority is to ensure public safety and build a modern, professional and people-oriented police force free from political influence, he said while addressing the graduation parade of the first phase of the 27th BCS (Police) batch at the Bangladesh Police Academy in Sardah, Rajshahi.
He said the government has taken various steps to restore the morale of the police force which was undermined by excessive politicisation during the previous “fascist government”.
The minister said a strict system of rewards for professionalism and disciplinary action for misconduct has been introduced to strengthen integrity and discipline within the force.
Congratulating the newly appointed officers who took part in the parade, the minister said this joyous moment should have come much earlier in their lives. He said it was deeply painful that they had endured 18 years of severe deprivation and inhumane suffering as victims of the vindictive actions of the previous authoritarian and fascist government.
The minister extended his heartfelt greetings to all the officers for regaining their rightful positions and due recognition following the fall of the authoritarian regime.
He said they were beginning their careers at a historic time for the country and urged them to uphold equality before the law.
“From political activists to marginal farmers, everyone is equal in the eyes of the law. No one seeking police services should face discrimination,” he added.
He also stressed the importance of maintaining the chain of command, discipline, loyalty and teamwork, while urging the officers to enhance their expertise in cyber security and criminal investigation to meet emerging challenges.
Reaffirming the government's zero-tolerance policy against corruption, Salahuddin called on all police members to perform their duties with honesty and dedication.
The minister expressed hope that members of the 27th BCS (Police) batch would use their knowledge and experience gained over the past 18 years in different professions to strengthen the Bangladesh Police.
A total of 58 probationary ASPs — 57 from the first phase of the 27th BCS (Police) batch and one from the 28th batch — officially entered service through the parade.
At the ceremony, Probationary ASP Dr Md Nurul Huda Bhuiyan won the Best in Field Activities award and was also named the Best Probationer. Probationary ASP ABM Mamun received the Best Shooter award, while Abu Numan Mohammad Khairul Islam won the Best Academic Award.
During the ceremony, the minister inspected the parade, took the salute and distributed awards among the best-performing probationary officers.
The event was attended as special guests by Land Minister Mizanur Rahman Minu, local Members of Parliament, Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md. Ali Hossain Fakir, Principal of Bangladesh Police Academy G M Azizur Rahman, Rajshahi Divisional Commissioner Dr. A.N.M. Bazlur Rashid, and Rajshahi Range Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Md. Ashik Saeed.
Senior military and civilian officials, local and foreign invited guests, guardians of the ASP probationers, and journalists from various media outlets were also present at the ceremony.

item.title: DB chief: Police tighten security for official vehicles over sabotage threat
item.description:
Bangladesh Police tightened security for official vehicles nationwide on Saturday following intelligence reports of possible sabotage, Detective Branch (DB) Chief of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Md Shafiqul Islam said on Sunday.
The clarification came on Sunday after journalists asked the DB Chief about the nationwide highest alert issued by Police Headquarters a day earlier.
Speaking at a press briefing at the DMP Media Centre, Shafiqul Islam said the directive was purely precautionary and aimed at ensuring the safety of police personnel and official vehicles.
"Recent bomb-related incidents and attempts to spread panic prompted senior officers to instruct field units to exercise greater vigilance," he said.
He added that police officers are responsible for safeguarding both themselves and government assets, and the latest directive simply reinforces existing security protocols.
"We are always alert. In light of the recent bomb scares, we have further strengthened our vigilance," the DB chief said.
On Saturday, Police Headquarters issued a nationwide highest alert after intelligence agencies warned of possible attacks on police vehicles, including jeeps, pickups and buses, by extremist members or other miscreants. Following the warning, all metropolitan, range, district and specialised police units were instructed to immediately tighten security.
The emergency directive stressed that there should be no lapse in ensuring the security of police vehicles, whether on duty or parked after duty hours.
It instructed officers to park vehicles only in secure locations during temporary stops and ensure they remain under constant supervision. Police vehicles must not be left unattended or without the designated driver or responsible officer under any circumstances.
The directive also called for enhanced security for all government vehicles stationed at police stations, police lines, office compounds and other designated facilities after duty hours. It further instructed units to intensify patrols, strengthen surveillance and remain alert to any suspicious persons or objects.
Describing the matter as "highly important," Police Headquarters directed all metropolitan, range, district and specialised units to strictly implement the security measures.

Md Zakir Anam new AMD of NCC Bank
item.description:
Md Zakir Anam has been promoted to the position of Additional Managing Director (AMD) of NCC Bank PLC.
Prior to his promotion, he served as deputy managing director, where he was responsible for corporate banking, international trade finance, remittance, and several other key divisions at the bank’s head office.
Since joining NCC Bank in October 2016, he has held a number of important leadership positions, including branch manager of Banani Branch as executive vice president and later branch manager of Gulshan Branch as senior executive vice president, making significant contributions to the bank’s business growth and operational excellence.
Md Zakir Anam began his banking career in 1995 with Prime Bank PLC.
He subsequently served with distinction as branch manager at various corporate branches of Exim Bank PLC, Al-Arafah Islami Bank PLC, and Midland Bank PLC.
He possesses more than 31 years of extensive experience in foreign trade, credit management, and branch banking.
Throughout his banking career, Anam has received numerous accolades in recognition of his outstanding performance and leadership, including the Chairman’s Best Manager Award, Appreciation Awards, and two Gold Medals.
He has also been honored with several other awards for his exceptional contributions to the banking industry.

item.title: Rancon Motor Bikes, MetLife Bangladesh to support safer riding for Suzuki buyers
item.description:
Rancon Motor Bikes Ltd has entered into a partnership with MetLife Bangladesh to provide complimentary insurance coverage to eligible Suzuki motorcycle buyers.
The initiative supports safer travel and responsible commuting for motorcycle riders in Bangladesh.
Under the partnership, customers who purchase new Suzuki motorcycles from authorized Rancon Motorbikes Limited dealers and flagship showroom points will receive one year of complimentary insurance coverage.
The coverage will commence from the date of purchase.
The complimentary insurance provides coverage in the event of accidental death or permanent disability, as defined in the policy.
Customers may also choose to enroll in a voluntary insurance plan which is available to both new and existing Suzuki motorcycle owners.
The voluntary plan offers additional coverage options, including accident-related medical expense reimbursement and daily hospital cash benefits for a limited period, subject to policy terms.
All claims are subject to policy conditions and standard assessment procedures.
The agreement was signed by Ala Uddin, additional managing director and CFO of MetLife Bangladesh, and Quazi Ashiq-Ur-Rahman, executive director of Rancon Motor Bikes Ltd., on behalf of their respective organizations.
Senior representatives from both companies were present at the signing ceremony.
This partnership reflects a shared focus on customer awareness, road safety, and access to insurance solutions.

item.title: Brac Bank's CORPnet records highest-ever monthly transaction volume of nearly Tk30,000cr
item.description:
Brac Bank's corporate internet banking platform, CORPnet, recorded its highest-ever monthly transaction volume in June 2026, processing nearly Tk30,000 crore as businesses increasingly embraced digital transaction banking.
Building on its record monthly performance, CORPnet processed more than Tk143,000 crore in transactions during the first six months of 2026.
This was 40% higher than the Tk102,000 crore processed during the same period last year.
The growth reflects the accelerating digitalization of corporate banking in Bangladesh.
During the first half of 2026, digital channels accounted for 80% of Brac Bank's corporate transactions, up from 74% a year earlier.
The platform also continued to attract more business users.
The number of corporate client groups using CORPnet increased by 40% year on year, while the total number of transactions rose by 43% to 5.24 million during the first six months of the year, highlighting deeper engagement with the bank's digital transaction banking platform.
Beyond transaction growth, CORPnet also strengthened its commercial proposition through the introduction of new digital capabilities.
Recently launched features such as A-Challan, A4 Cheque Printing and Pay Order Issuance have expanded the platform's value proposition for corporate clients.
The platform now also enables corporates to pay Titas utility bills digitally in real time, reducing reliance on manual processes and branch visits.
Its collection solution through Virtual Accounts recorded 20% year-on-year growth in collection volume during the first half of 2026, helping businesses automate receivables reconciliation, accelerate collections, and improve working capital management.
Commenting on the milestone, Md Shaheen Iqbal, additional managing director and head of wholesale banking at Brac Bank, said: "The record transaction volume demonstrates how rapidly businesses are adopting digital banking to manage their day-to-day financial operations. At Brac Bank, we continue to invest in technology and innovation to deliver secure, efficient and scalable transaction banking solutions that help our clients operate with greater speed, control and convenience."
CORPnet is Brac Bank's corporate internet banking platform that enables businesses to manage payments, collections, liquidity and other banking transactions through a secure digital interface.
The platform forms a key part of the bank's broader strategy to advance digital transaction banking and deliver a seamless banking experience for corporate customers.

item.title: Experts urge withdrawal of proposal to raise foreign ownership cap in logistics
item.description:
Policymakers, entrepreneurs and researchers have called for the withdrawal of a proposal in the draft Freight Forwarding Rules to raise the foreign ownership ceiling from 40% to 49%.
The call came at a roundtable, "Protecting Domestic Investment in Logistics & Policy Reform", organized by the Center for Strategic Research (CSR) at the Brac Centre in Mohakhali, Dhaka, on Wednesday.
Zonayed Saki, State Minister for Planning, joined online as chief guest; Mahmudur Rahman Manna, president of Nagorik Oikya, attended as special guest.
The concept paper was presented by Saqeeb Anwer, executive director of CSR.
He said freight forwarding, shipping agency, customs agency and courier-express require little fixed capital to operate. Foreign ownership therefore brings no factories, equipment or technology — only a licence, through which existing cargo flows shift into the owner's own global network. What takes place in the market, he said, is substitution rather than competition.
The paper noted that Bangladesh spends at least $9 billion a year on freight, of which domestic vessels capture only 8% to 10%; with a larger fleet, around $2 billion could be retained onshore. After the Bangladesh Flag Vessels (Protection of Interest) Act 2019, the domestic ocean-going flag fleet grew from 48 vessels to 80.
Section 9(4) of the Civil Aviation Act 2017, which requires a foreign airline's agent to be wholly owned by a Bangladeshi citizen, has built a fully domestic GSA industry. Saqeeb Anwer said that although many wholly foreign-owned companies operate here, none has invested in a domestic vessel or in infrastructure.
Concern was expressed that the Shipping Agent and C&F Agent Licensing Rules have both cut the 60/40 structure to 51/49; that the current budget has withdrawn the 49% cap on ICDs and off-docks; and that courier services carry no cap at all.
The 60/40 structure in the freight forwarding rules is therefore the last remaining benchmark for domestic ownership.
The validity of licence renewals for wholly foreign-owned companies is also pending before the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 12489/2019; amending the rules before the rule nisi is disposed of could render the proceedings ineffective, speakers said.
Describing logistics as a sensitive sector tied to national security, Fazle Huda, MP for Naogaon-3, said many foreign firms take large sums of foreign exchange out of the country merely by issuing bills of lading and other documents, without visible infrastructure.
"We are not against foreign investment," he said. "But that investment must go into infrastructure — railways, cold chain, modern trucks and agriculture-based supply systems." Citing restrictions in Sri Lanka and India, he said a sector tied to trade, ports and internal security must be treated as strategic, and that the practice of running businesses behind nominal local partners arranged through lawyers or consultants must end.
Kabir Ahmed, president of IAEAB and adviser to BAFFA, said around 80% of the country's freight business is controlled by foreign firms, yet most bring no meaningful FDI.
Md Ariful Ahsan, president of Baffa, warned that continued over-dependence would weaken the domestic logistics industry.
Shafiqul Alam, editor of Daily Waadaa, said global realities and geopolitics must inform how foreign investment is sought, and that it may not be necessary in every sector.
Mahmudur Rahman Manna said excessive foreign participation is depriving domestic entrepreneurs of opportunity, and that the concealment in this sector needs far more open discussion.
ATM Azizul Akil David, former senior vice president of the Bangladesh China Chamber of Commerce and Industry, said effective interest rates reaching 23% to 24% are forcing domestic entrepreneurs out of business while foreign firms enjoy a comparative advantage.
Six demands were placed from the roundtable: a uniform 60/40 structure across all four sub-sectors, with domestic majority applied to shares, dividend rights and board voting; uniform and strict enforcement of existing rules at renewal; a minimum paid-up capital of $5 to $10 million for firms with foreign participation, of which at least 40% must be shown within 24 months as real investment in warehousing, equipment and transport fleet; foreign hiring limited to senior management; assessment of foreign exchange outflow as a precondition of licence renewal; and mandatory declaration of beneficial ownership to curb nominee holdings.
Also taking part were Abu Alam Md Shahid Khan, former secretary; Barrister M Saquibuzzaman; Mahmud Hosain, former vice president of ICAB, Hasan Mamun, consulting editor of Dhaka Stream; and Kamruzzaman, head of finance at Rifline Logistics.

David Emon, 3 associates placed on 10-day remand in 2 cases
item.description:
A Chittagong court on Sunday placed listed top criminal Mobarak Hossain Emon alias David Emon, and his three associates on 10 days' remand in murder and arms cases filed at Fatikchhari Police Station in Chattogram.
Judge of the Senior Judicial Magistrate-3 Motasim Billah passed the order when police produced the four accused before his court, seeking seven days' remand in each of the two cases.
The other accused placed on remand are Md Shamim, Safayet Hossain and Al Islam Alif, also known as Tamal.
After hearing both sides, the court granted five days' remand in each case, totalling 10 days.
On Thursday, another Chittagong court sent David Emon and three associates to jail after showing them arrested in three cases.
David Emon was arrested in a joint operation in Jessore in the early hours of July 29 while trying to flee to India.
Earlier in the day, the accused were produced before the court under tight security. Additional police were deployed in and around the court premises during the remand hearing.
According to case documents, police recovered firearms from Fatikchhari on July 29 based on information obtained from Emon and three others following their arrest.
Police said David Emon, 25, son of late Md Musa of Kanchannagar in Fatikchhari upazila, faces 13 cases, including those related to murder and illegal arms.
Additional Superintendent of Police (Hathazari Circle) Kazi Md Tareq Aziz said the accused will be questioned to gather further information about their criminal activities and to recover more illegal weapons.
According to multiple district police sources, investigators traced David Emon's whereabouts while probing the murder of Maksudul Haque Chowdhury in the Pahartali area on June 13.
Based on information provided by the arrested suspects, police later raided an abandoned house in Manikpur village of Kanchannagor union in Fatikchhari and recovered a foreign pistol, two local LG guns and several other improvised weapons.

No respite for Dhaka consumers as food prices soar
item.description:
As households struggle to cope with rising living costs, there is little sign of relief in Dhaka's kitchen markets, where the prices of rice, vegetables, fish, eggs and poultry continue to edge higher.
After visiting several kitchen markets across Dhaka on Saturday, it was found that, except for a few varieties, almost all vegetables were selling for around Tk100 per kg, while green chilli prices had soared to Tk400 per kg.
Rice prices have also resumed their upward trend, with polao rice registering the sharpest increase. Traders said its price has jumped by Tk50–60 per kg within just a few days, adding to the burden on consumers already coping with a gas supply crisis.
According to traders, persistent rainfall and flooding in several parts of the country have submerged vegetable and chilli fields, disrupted supplies and increased transportation costs. The seasonal decline in supply during the monsoon has also contributed to higher prices of most essential commodities.
Fish prices have risen by Tk20–30 per kg over the past week. Pangas is now selling at Tk250 per kg, telapia at Tk280, rui at Tk300–450, pabda at Tk350–400, shrimp at Tk800–1,400, tengra at Tk700, indigenous koi at Tk700–800 and shoal at Tk700 per kg. Prices of bhetki, mrigel, baim, shing and poa fish have also increased.
Hilsa is being sold at Tk1,600–3,200 per kg, depending on its size and quality, while prices of sea fish have also climbed beyond the reach of many middle- and low-income consumers.
Anwar Hossain, a fish vendor at Dhupkhola Kitchen Market, said adverse weather has kept many fishing trawlers from going to sea, while supplies from different parts of the country have declined.
"Wholesale prices have increased due to lower supply, and that has inevitably pushed up retail prices," he said.
Consumers say persistently high food prices are forcing them to rethink their spending, with fish and meat becoming increasingly unaffordable.
"My children wanted to eat fish, but I was shocked by the prices at the market," said shopper Jony Sheikh. "I somehow managed to buy one fish for them. If prices keep rising, we'll have to cut back on fish and meat."
Green chilli prices have surged to Tk400 per kg across Dhaka's kitchen markets, up by around Tk100 from a week ago. Retailers are charging Tk40 for 100 grams and Tk100 for 250 grams.
Locally produced onions have also become costlier, rising by Tk15–20 per kg over the past one-and-a-half to two weeks. Depending on quality, they are now selling for Tk55–65 per kg.
Vegetable prices remain high, with long brinjal selling for Tk120–150 per kg, round brinjal Tk180, white brinjal Tk140, bitter gourd Tk120–140, yardlong beans Tk110–130, snake gourd Tk90–100 and taro corms Tk80–100 per kg. Only sponge gourd and pointed gourd offered some relief, with prices easing to Tk60–80 per kg. Rafique, a vegetable vendor, blamed the price hike on supply shortages caused by heavy rains and flooding.
"Supplies from different parts of the country have declined during the monsoon, while waterlogging has damaged chilli fields in major producing areas. Reduced supply has pushed up prices," he said.
Sridevi Biswas, a shopper at Ray Saheb Bazar, said she had planned to buy several vegetables but returned home with only one.
"I came to buy a few vegetables, but after seeing the prices I bought only one. If this trend continues, it will become even harder for middle-income families to manage their household expenses," she said. Egg prices have also moved up, with farm eggs now selling for Tk145–155 per dozen, compared with Tk135–140 a week ago.
Poultry prices also increased over the past day. Broiler chicken is now selling for Tk190–200 per kg, up from Tk180, while Sonali chicken has risen to Tk340–350 per kg from Tk330–340.
Robin Hasan, a university student living in a shared accommodation, said eggs and chicken had long been the most affordable protein options.
"Even those are becoming more expensive now. Managing within a limited budget is getting harder every day," he said.
While prices of coarse, medium-grade and Miniket rice have remained largely stable, polao rice has seen a sharp spike.
Coarse rice is selling for Tk58–65 per kg, medium-grade rice for Tk68–78, and Miniket and Nazirshail varieties for Tk80–95 per kg.
In contrast, polao rice, which sold for Tk120–140 per kg just a few days ago, is now priced at Tk180–200 per kg, marking an increase of Tk50–60 per kg.
Traders said the jump is the steepest increase in the rice market in recent weeks, adding to the financial strain on consumers already grappling with the rising cost of living.

Four killed in pickup-truck collision in Bogra
item.description:
Four people, including a pickup van driver, were killed in a head-on collision between a pickup van and a goods-laden truck in Bogra's Kahaloo upazila on Saturday morning.
The accident occurred in the Kazipara Boubazar area of Birkedar union along the Bogra–Naogaon highway.
The deceased were identified as Toriqul Islam Riyad, 23, son of Ferdous Islam of Pachashi village in Gouripur upazila; pickup driver Nasir Uddin, 24, son of the late Amin Khan of the same village; Lutfor Rahman, 50, son of Toyeb Ali of Raghabpur in Mymensingh Sadar; and Shubha Debnath, 23, son of Chittaranjan Debnath of the same area.
According to family members, the three fish traders had travelled from Mymensingh to Adamdighi in Bogra with a consignment of fish fry for sale. After selling the fish, they were returning home when the accident occurred.
Police said the crash occurred around 10:00 am when the pickup van attempted to overtake a bus and collided head-on with a Naogaon-bound truck coming from the opposite direction, killing the driver and three fish traders on the spot.
The accident briefly disrupted traffic on the Bogra–Naogaon highway. Fire Service and Civil Defence personnel, assisted by police, recovered the bodies and removed the wrecked vehicles, allowing traffic to resume.
Sub-Inspector Brojer Mahato of Kahaloo Police Station said the victims included three fish traders and the pickup driver. The pickup van and the truck have been seized, while the truck driver and his assistant fled the scene.
"The victims' families in Mymensingh have been informed. The bodies will be handed over to their relatives upon arrival," he said.
Officer-in-Charge (OC) Shafiqul Islam said a case has been filed under the Road Transport Act, and efforts are underway to arrest the absconding truck driver.

DSCC showcases fridges, TVs, sofas recovered from Dhaka drains
item.description:
Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) on Saturday staged an unusual awareness procession featuring refrigerators, televisions, sofas, mattresses, polythene and plastic waste recovered from drains to demonstrate how indiscriminate waste disposal contributes to waterlogging and environmental pollution in the capital.
The "Waste Procession" was inaugurated at Shahbagh by DSCC Administrator Md Abdus Salam, alongside the launch of the corporation's monthly "Cleaning Day," observed simultaneously across all 75 wards.
Speaking at the event, the DSCC administrator said Dhaka cannot become a clean and green city without greater public awareness and civic responsibility.
"If everyone fulfills their responsibilities, a large part of the city's waterlogging, waste management and environmental pollution problems can be controlled," he said.
Urging residents not to blame the city corporation alone for waterlogging, he said citizens also have a responsibility to dispose of waste properly.
"Even a single polythene bag or a discarded mattress can block a drain and cause waterlogging across an entire neighborhood," he said, calling on residents not to dump waste into drains.
Abdus Salam said changing public behavior is essential if Dhaka is to shed its reputation as one of the world's most polluted cities.
"If we do not become conscious ourselves, it will not be possible to protect Dhaka," he added.
He also said dustbins are being reinstalled across the city under the prime minister's directive after many previously installed bins were stolen. He urged business owners to place waste bins in front of their establishments, saying there is no excuse for indiscriminate dumping.
The administrator announced that a special crash program on mosquito control and waste management will be carried out on the first Saturday of every month across all 75 DSCC wards.
Alongside routine cleaning activities, the initiative will focus on clearing clogged drains and cleaning neglected areas. He also invited social, voluntary and political organizations to participate.
Highlighting the importance of environmental protection, Abdus Salam stressed the need for extensive tree planting, saying it is essential to reduce carbon dioxide levels and increase oxygen.
He also praised volunteers from Bidyanondo Foundation for their community service, saying a cleaner, more livable Dhaka requires collective efforts from citizens, the media and civil society.
Following the inauguration, participants marched through several roads carrying waste recovered from drains to demonstrate the consequences of improper waste disposal. They also distributed awareness leaflets explaining the causes of waterlogging, proper waste management practices and the harmful effects of plastic pollution.
DSCC Chief Executive Officer Md Khairur Rahman attended the event as a special guest. Bidyanondo Foundation Executive Director Md Jamal Uddin, environmental activists, students, volunteers, DSCC officials and media representatives were also present.

Road crashes killed 1,384 in Dhaka since 2020
item.description:
A total of 1,384 people were killed and 2,488 others injured in 1,849 road crashes across the capital between January 2020 and July 2026, according to data released by the Road Safety Foundation on Saturday.
The analysis found that 1,034 of those killed were men (74.71%), 219 were women (15.82%), and 131 were children (9.46%).
Year-wise data showed that 126 people were killed and 233 injured in 124 crashes in 2020. The figures rose to 141 deaths and 247 injuries in 137 crashes in 2021, followed by 256 deaths and 324 injuries in 268 crashes in 2022.
In 2023, 249 people were killed and 335 injured in 296 crashes. The following year, 246 people died and 482 were injured in 394 crashes. In 2025, 229 people were killed and 511 injured in 407 crashes. Up to July 2026, 137 people had been killed and 356 injured in 223 crashes.
Of those killed, 592 (42.77%) were pedestrians, 536 (38.72%) were motorcyclists, and 256 (18.49%) were drivers or passengers of buses, rickshaws, CNG-run auto-rickshaws, and other vehicles.
Most fatalities occurred at night, accounting for 519 deaths (37.5%). The remaining deaths were recorded in the morning (258), afternoon (195), evening (174), early morning (142), and at dusk (96).
Heavy vehicles—including trucks, covered vans, pickups, tankers, and garbage trucks—were involved in the highest proportion of crashes (33.25%), followed by motorcycles (26%), buses (21.75%), auto-rickshaws, CNG-run auto-rickshaws, and legunas (12.73%), and microbuses, private cars, and jeeps (6.25%).
The Road Safety Foundation said road crashes occur more frequently at night and in the morning in the capital. It attributed the trend to heavy goods vehicles traveling at high speeds during nighttime due to the absence of bypass roads, exposing pedestrians to greater risk while crossing roads.
The organization also blamed chronic traffic congestion, inadequate road infrastructure, mixed traffic, encroached footpaths, a shortage of usable footbridges, and poor road-user awareness for the high number of crashes and fatalities.
It identified Jatrabari, Demra, Mohammadpur, Kuril World Road, and Airport Road as major crash hotspots.
The foundation recommended introducing company-based bus services through route rationalization to improve discipline in Dhaka's public transport system. It also called for coordinated action by the Bangladesh Road Transport Authority (BRTA), Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation (BRTC), Dhaka Transport Coordination Authority (DTCA), the two city corporations, and the traffic police.

item.title: Businessman dies after assault in Khilgaon
item.description:
A 40-year-old businessman died after being beaten allegedly by a group of unidentified assailants in the capital's Khilgaon area, police said on Saturday
The deceased was identified as Kamruzzaman Khan Dipu, who ran a water supply business. He was the son of Md Sams Uddin and a resident of 721/1/A, Block C, Khilgaon, said Sub-Inspector (SI) Sumon Mia of Khilgaon Police Station.
Police recovered the body from Mugda General Hospital around 10pm on Friday. After completing the required legal formalities, the body was sent to the Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) morgue, where an autopsy was conducted on Saturday.
According to police, witnesses said 10 to 12 unidentified men assaulted Dipu around 7pm on July 29 before leaving him critically injured near the Khilgaon Rail Gate.
He was first taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where doctors advised immediate admission to the intensive care unit (ICU). However, no ICU bed was available, and his family could not afford treatment at a private hospital. They later took him home.
His condition deteriorated, and he was taken to Mugda General Hospital around 7:45pm on Friday, where the duty doctor declared him dead.
Police said an investigation was underway, and legal action will be taken based on its findings.

item.title: Swapon: Humanitarian philosophy essential to rebuild nation after fascism
item.description:
Information and Broadcasting Minister Jahir Uddin Swapon on Saturday said the chapter of ousting fascism has ended and the country must now focus on rebuilding the state, strengthening democratic institutions and fostering a society rooted in humanity, tolerance and mutual respect.
Speaking as the chief guest at a discussion and photo exhibition titled "Bangladesh in the Face of Bullets, Fascism Came to an End" at the National Press Club, Swapon said the movement had achieved its objectives of restoring democracy and ensuring people's voting rights.
"The phase of toppling fascism is over. Now is the time to build the country," he said. "The movement was aimed at restoring democracy and securing the people's right to vote. We must now rebuild the state, strengthen democratic institutions and work together to fulfil the aspirations of the people."
The minister said the country's journey towards restoring democracy had been shaped by a prolonged popular movement. While crediting the people with the success of the movement, he said BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman had provided leadership and strategic direction from abroad.
Swapon said Tarique Rahman never claimed personal credit for the mass uprising, instead consistently describing it as a victory of the people and working to keep pro-democracy forces united throughout the movement.
He said two slogans popularised by Tarique Rahman"If you are afraid, you are finished; if you stand up, you are Bangladesh" and "The country's future will be decided on the streets" injected fresh momentum into the movement, which culminated in the August 5 mass uprising.
The minister said that with the national election concluded, the country now needs politics centred on nation-building rather than confrontation. He stressed the need to strengthen democratic practices, ensure an effective parliamentary system and uphold responsible governance to meet public expectations.
He said that while political movements might become a profession for some, their struggle had always been aimed at restoring democracy, safeguarding voting rights and building an independent and sovereign Bangladesh. With those goals achieved, he added, the focus should now shift to development and state-building.
Highlighting the importance of preserving the history of the anti-fascist movement, Swapon said photographs taken by photojournalists would remain enduring records of the struggle for democracy for future generations.

item.title: IOM deputy DG arrives in Dhaka on four-day visit
item.description:
The International Organization for Migration's (IOM) Deputy Director General for Operations, Ugochi Daniels , arrived in Dhaka on Saturday on a four-day official visit to Bangladesh.
She was received at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport by IOM Regional Director for Asia and the Pacific Iori Kato , United Nations Resident Coordinator in Bangladesh Carol Flore-Smereczniak , and IOM Chief of Mission in Bangladesh Dr Laura Tomm Bonde .
During the visit, Daniels is scheduled to meet senior government officials, UN partners, donors, and communities supported by IOM.
She will also attend the launch of Bangladesh's National Action Plan 2026–2030 for the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration (GCM).
As part of her itinerary, Daniels will travel to Cox's Bazar and Madaripur to engage with stakeholders on migration governance, climate mobility, labor migration, protection, and humanitarian response.

item.title: Indian passenger held in suspected gold smuggling at Shah Amanat Airport
item.description:
Customs Intelligence and Investigation Directorate (CIID) officials have detained an Indian passenger at Chattogram’s Shah Amanat International Airport after recovering capsule-like objects containing gold.
Acting on a tip-off, a team from the CIID regional office in Chattogram intercepted the passenger after he crossed the green channel at the airport on Saturday morning.
The passenger, identified as Thamim Ansari, arrived from Sharjah in the United Arab Emirates on Air Arabia flight G9-526, which landed at 6:58 am.
During a body search, officials recovered capsule-shaped packets containing gold concealed inside his underwear.
Authorities said the exact quantity and purity of the gold are being determined with the assistance of a certified goldsmith after removing the packing materials.
The recovered gold is estimated to be worth around Tk 1 crore, officials said.
CIID said legal action is being taken against the passenger under the Customs Act, while steps are also underway to file a criminal case in connection with the smuggling attempt.
The agency said it would continue intelligence surveillance and enforcement drives to prevent the smuggling of gold and other contraband through the country’s international airports.

item.description:
State Minister for Railways Habibur Rashid has announced that a new pair of intercity trains will be launched on the Dhaka–Cox's Bazar route later this month to meet growing passenger demand and ease ticket shortages.
The announcement came during his visit to the Cox's Bazar Railway Station on Saturday morning.
The state minister said the number of passengers and tourists travelling to Cox's Bazar has been increasing steadily, prompting the government to expand rail services and modernize passenger facilities.
He expressed hope that the new train pair would significantly reduce passenger suffering, ease ticket pressure and ensure a more comfortable, convenient and timely journey on the route.
Rashid also said the government plans to transform the Cox's Bazar Railway Station into an international-standard, tourism-friendly rail hub.
As part of this initiative, the full operation and management of the station will be entrusted to a private organization to ensure efficient and high-quality services.
During the visit, the state minister inspected various sections of the station and reviewed passenger services, infrastructure, cleanliness, security arrangements and overall operational activities.
He instructed the concerned officials to expedite the full opening of the station and ensure international-standard services for passengers.
Cox's Bazar Sadar MP Lutfur Rahman, senior railway officials and officials of the Cox's Bazar Railway Station were present during the visit.

item.title: 43% of Aman seedling transplantation completed in Rangpur region
item.description:
Aman rice transplantation has been completed on 43% of the target farmland in the Rangpur agricultural region, with farmers continuing planting in full swing amid favourable monsoon rainfall.
According to the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE), Aman seedlings have so far been transplanted on 267,267 hectares of land out of the targeted 621,550 hectares across the region.
Md Shirajul Islam, additional director of the DAE for Rangpur region, expressed optimism that the cultivation target would be achieved this season as weather conditions remain favourable.
The DAE has set a production target of 2.01 million tonnes of clean Aman rice (3.01 million tonnes in paddy equivalent) from 621,550 hectares across Rangpur, Gaibandha, Kurigram, Lalmonirhat and Nilphamari districts.
The target includes 1.67 million tonnes of high-yielding Aman rice from 524,520 hectares, 314,221 tonnes of hybrid Aman rice from 86,020 hectares, and 20,737 tonnes of local Aman rice from 11,010 hectares.
Last season, farmers produced 2.00 million tonnes of clean Aman rice from 616,299 hectares in the region.
Farmers have prepared seedbeds on 34,586 hectares—13.77% more than the required 30,401 hectares—to ensure an adequate supply of seedlings.
The government, through the DAE, has distributed quality Aman seeds and fertilisers among small and marginal farmers. Authorities have also prepared contingency plans, including late-variety and floating seedbeds, to address any seedling shortages in the event of flooding in August.
"We have instructed field-level agricultural officers to provide all necessary support and modern technologies to ensure successful Aman cultivation this season," Shirajul Islam said.
Farmers across Sadar, Gangachara, Taraganj, Mithapukur and Pirgachha upazilas said transplantation had gained momentum following frequent seasonal rainfall.
"We are hopeful of achieving the Aman cultivation target this season," said farmer Mofizar Rahman of Taraganj.
Another farmer, Anwar Hossain of Gangachara, said the young Aman plants were growing well due to the recent rains.

Green chili at Tk400; most vegetables now above Tk100
item.description:
Persistent rainfall and flooding across the country have sent the prices of essential commodities soaring in Dhaka, squeezing already strained household budgets and deepening the hardship for low- and middle-income families.
After visiting several markets in the capital on Friday, it was found that beef prices remained stable, the prices of fish, eggs, onions, green chillies and most vegetables had risen sharply, with many selling at around Tk100 per kilogram or more.
Traders blamed the price hike on supply disruptions caused by heavy rains and floods, which have affected the production and transportation of agricultural produce and fish. They said higher wholesale prices, rising transport costs and reduced output in flood-hit areas had pushed up retail prices.
Market visits showed that the prices of most fish varieties had increased by Tk20-30 per kilogram over the past week. Pangas, often regarded as an affordable fish, was selling at Tk230 per kg, while telapia was priced at Tk260. Rui is being sold at Tk300-450 per kg, pabda at Tk350-400, shrimp at Tk800-900, tengra at Tk700, native koi at Tk700-800 and shoal at Tk700. Prices of vetki, mrigel, baim, shing and poa also increased.
Sea fish prices remained significantly higher. Anwar Hossain, a fish trader at Dhupkhola Market, said hilsa was selling for Tk1,600-3,200 per kg depending on size and quality, while pomfret was priced at Tk1,200-1,300, red coral at Tk1,000-1,200, tuna at Tk850-1,000 and surma at Tk700 per kg. Prices may vary slightly from market to market, he added.
Meanwhile, the price of green chillies climbed to Tk400 per kilogram, up by around Tk100 from a week earlier Lal Mia, a vegetable vendor at Narinda Kitchen Market, said retail prices of green chilies had jumped sharply over the past week as wholesale rates continued to rise.
"Last week, I sold green chilies at Tk 280–300 per kg. Now, wholesale prices have increased significantly, forcing us to sell them at Tk 400 per kg," he said.
He attributed the price hike to prolonged rainfall, which has inundated vegetable fields across several parts of the country, disrupting supply.
"Most vegetable fields have gone under water due to the rains, resulting in lower market supplies. Consequently, the prices of almost all vegetables, except a few, have increased," he added.
The onion market has also turned volatile. Locally produced onions, which were selling for Tk 40–45 per kg about one and a half to two weeks ago, are now retailing at Tk 55–65 per kg, depending on quality.
Enamul Haque, a vendor at Raysaheb Bazar said, "Onions that we were selling for Tk 40 per kg are now retailing at Tk 60 or even more because wholesale prices have risen unexpectedly."
There has been little respite in the vegetable market, with most produce now selling at around Tk 100 per kg or higher. Long eggplants are priced at Tk 120–150 per kg, round eggplants Tk 180, white eggplants Tk 140, bitter gourds Tk 120–140, yardlong beans Tk 110–130, snake gourds Tk 90–100, and taro corms Tk 80–100 per kg. However, prices of sponge gourds and pointed gourds have eased slightly to Tk 60–80 per kg.
Egg prices have also increased over the past week. Farm eggs are now selling at Tk 145–155 per dozen, up from Tk 135–140 a week earlier. In contrast, broiler chicken prices have remained relatively stable at Tk 180–190 per kg, while Sonali chicken is being sold at Tk 330–340 per kg.
Beef prices have remained unchanged, with beef retailing at Tk 750–800 per kg and mutton at Tk 1,100–1,200 per kg.
Consumers said persistent rainfall, flooding and supply disruptions have driven up the prices of essential commodities, placing additional pressure on low- and middle-income households already struggling with rising living costs.
Md Jahangir Alam, a rickshaw puller, said a significant portion of his daily earnings now goes toward buying food.
"A large share of my daily income is spent at the market. I used to buy fish once or twice a week, but now I struggle to make ends meet even after buying eggs and vegetables. When a basic item like green chili costs Tk 400 per kg, it becomes extremely difficult for people like us," he said.
Nasrin Akter, a shopper at Dhupkhola Market, said the simultaneous increase in the prices of green chilies, eggs, onions and vegetables had further strained household budgets.
"Just a few days ago, I bought a dozen eggs for Tk 135–140. Now I have to pay around Tk 150. Every trip to the market forces us to revise our budget. These prices are becoming increasingly difficult for ordinary families to bear," she said.

item.title: Three held with 464 weapons at Baitul Mukarram
item.description:
Police arrested three people and seized a large cache of locally made weapons and other equipment during a special drive at Link Road adjacent to the Baitul Mukarram Gold Market in the capital on Thursday.
The arrestees were identified as Robiul Islam, 40, Md Azad, 30, and Md Rajan, 34.
Harun Or Rashid, deputy commissioner of the Motijheel Division of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP), said the operation was launched to curb the illegal sale of sharp weapons used in muggings, violent crimes and other criminal activities in the capital.
During the raid, police recovered a total of 464 weapons and related items, including machetes, large knives, switchblade knives, combat knives, electric stun guns, Chinese axes, baton sticks and toy pistols designed to resemble real firearms.
According to preliminary interrogation, the seized weapons and equipment had been stockpiled for sale to individuals involved in criminal activities across different parts of the capital.

item.title: DNCC administrator vows action against unfit vehicles, unskilled drivers
item.description:
Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) Administrator Md Safiqul Islam Khan on Friday said strict legal action will be taken against unfit vehicles and unlicensed or unskilled drivers in coordination with the Bangladesh Road Transport Authority (BRTA).
He made the remarks while visiting the house of DNCC conservancy worker Shefali Begum, who was killed in a road accident while on duty in the Madhya Badda area earlier in the day.
After learning of the tragic road accident, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman instructed the authorities to immediately visit the residence of the deceased sanitation worker.
Following the directive, State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives Mir Shahe Alam, State Minister for Housing and Public Works Ahammad Sohel Monzoor and the DNCC administrator rushed to the victim's home.
Safiqul said action will also be taken against anyone found driving DNCC vehicles without proper skills or if any helper is found driving a vehicle after an investigation.
He said conservancy workers work day and night to keep the city clean and urged everyone to ensure their safety while performing their duties.
The DNCC announced Tk4 lakh in financial assistance and one year’s salary for Shefali’s family.
The administrator expressed condolences to the bereaved family and called on reckless drivers to exercise caution to prevent road accidents.
DNCC Chief Waste Management Officer Commodore Mohammad Humayun Kabir and other officials were present during the visit.

Female nursing student found dead in Dhaka hostel
item.description:
Police recovered the hanging body of a female nursing student from a hostel in the Kalabagan area of the capital on Friday morning.
Pinki Biswas, 19, was the daughter of Prafulla Biswas of Jambari village under Wazirpur upazila in Barisal district.
Sub-Inspector of Kalabagan Police Station Liza Akhter said police recovered the body around 8:30am after breaking open the door of a room at the hostel on the Crescent Road.
She was found hanging from a ceiling fan with a rope tied around her neck. The body was later sent to the Dhaka Medical College Hospital morgue for an autopsy.
Pinki was a first-year student at Anwer Khan Modern Nursing College. She shared the room with two other students, who were on leave.
The exact cause of the death will be known after the autopsy, Liza added.

item.title: Three killed in bus-truck collision in Tangail
item.description:
Three people, including a child, were killed and at least 17 others were injured after a passenger bus collided with a truck in Madhupur upazila of Tangail at around 10pm on Thursday.
The accident occurred in the Raktipara area on the Tangail–Mymensingh highway. The identities of the deceased could not be confirmed immediately.
Police and members of the Madhupur Fire Service said a Crown Deluxe passenger bus was travelling from Dhaka to Madarganj when it collided with a sand-laden truck heading toward Tangail after reaching the Raktipara area.
Three people, including a child, were killed on the spot, while at least 17 others sustained injuries. Fire Service personnel rescued 4 injured people and sent them to a hospital.
Mohammad Borhan Ali, station officer of Madhupur Fire Service, said: “After receiving the information, we recovered the bodies and handed them over to the police.”
AKM Fazlul Haque, officer-in-charge of Madhupur Police Station, said: “We are trying to identify the deceased. After completing the legal procedures, the bodies will be handed over to their relatives.”

item.title: GAU secures patent for jackfruit seed mineral concentrate technology
item.description:
Gazipur Agricultural University (GAU) has developed a patented technology to produce a mineral-rich food ingredient from jackfruit seeds, transforming an underutilised agricultural by-product into a value-added nutritional resource with potential applications in the food industry.
The innovation, jointly developed by Professor Dr Md Emdadul Haque of the Department of Food Engineering and postgraduate researcher Md Akram Hossain, has been granted a patent by the Department of Patents, Designs and Trademarks (DPDT) under the Ministry of Industries. The patent is registered as P/BD/2024/000040.
The invention, completed in November 2025 after three years of research under the guidance of GAU Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr GKM Mostafizur Rahman, is the university's first patented technology since it was renamed Gazipur Agricultural University. It also brings the institution's total number of patented technologies to 21.
The research was funded through the Ministry of Education's Grants for Advanced Research and Education (GARE) project.
According to the researchers, the technology increases the mineral concentration of dried jackfruit seeds from about 2% to more than 33%—a 16- to 17-fold increase—creating a concentrated ingredient suitable for use in fortified and processed foods.
Bangladesh is among the world's leading producers of jackfruit, yet large quantities of seeds and other by-products are discarded each year. The researchers said the technology offers a sustainable way to reduce food waste while creating new opportunities for value addition in the country's agro-processing sector.
The mineral concentrate contains essential nutrients, including potassium, calcium, magnesium, phosphorus, iron, zinc and manganese, which are vital for bone health, blood formation, immune function, and normal muscle and nerve function.
"The mineral concentrate can be incorporated into processed foods to enhance their nutritional value while reducing agricultural waste and supporting food and nutrition security," said Professor Dr Emdadul Haque.
He added that commercialising the technology could accelerate the development of nutrient-enriched food products, expand jackfruit-based industries, increase farmers' incomes and promote more efficient utilisation of agricultural resources.
GAU Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr GKM Mostafizur Rahman described the patent as "a milestone for Bangladesh's agricultural, food and nutrition research," saying it demonstrates how agricultural waste can be transformed into a high-value nutritional resource.

item.title: Heavy rains ravage Faridpur chilli fields, prices soar
item.description:
Prolonged heavy rainfall has devastated summer chilli cultivation in Faridpur's Madhukhali upazila, destroying large swathes of farmland, leaving thousands of growers counting heavy losses, and pushing retail prices of the spice to as high as Tk320 per kilogram.
Once carpeted with lush green chilli plants, fields across the upazila now lie waterlogged after more than a week of incessant rain, with rotting plants and failed crops replacing what had promised to be a productive season.
Madhukhali Upazila Agriculture Officer Md Mahbub Elahi said summer chilli was cultivated on around 2,720 hectares this season, but excessive rainfall submerged most fields, causing widespread crop damage.
"Waterlogging has caused chilli plants to rot and die in most of the cultivated areas. We are preparing a list of affected farmers. Some have already received government assistance, while others will be brought under compensation programmes in phases," he said.
According to local farmers, nearly three-quarters of the chilli fields have been damaged, with Raipur, Jahapur and Meghchami unions suffering the worst losses.
Farmers, including Rokonuzzaman and Firoz Mia of Raipur Union, said they had no option but to uproot their crops after the plants died.
"Almost all our chilli plants have perished due to the heavy rain. We have been forced to clear the fields," they said.
They said cultivation costs had already risen sharply because of higher prices of seeds, fertilisers and pesticides. With the crop wiped out, many farmers are unlikely to recover even half of their investment.
"If the government provides financial support, we will be able to resume cultivation," they added.
According to the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE), chilli has been cultivated on 3,112 hectares across Faridpur district this season, with a production target of 5,706 tonnes. Officials now fear the target will not be met because of the widespread damage caused by continuous rainfall.
The production shortfall has also driven up prices in local markets.
A visit to Haji Shariatullah Market, Chakbazar, Tepakhola Market and Helipad Market in Faridpur town found green chilli retailing at Tk280-Tk320 per kg, depending on quality.
Retail traders said supplies had fallen sharply as rain-damaged fields yielded little produce, resulting in steep price increases.
Faridpur Krishak Samity President Advocate Manik Majumdar urged the government to provide immediate compensation and rehabilitation support to affected farmers.
"There is hardly any chilli left in the fields, yet prices continue to climb. If affected farmers are not supported quickly, many may be discouraged from cultivating chilli next season," he said.

626 Bangladeshis experience 'auto-cancellation' of UAE visas; renewal process underway
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam on Thursday said exactly 626 Bangladeshis, not 5,000, have experienced "auto-cancellation" of their visas so far, and the government is closely working with the government of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) for their visa renewals.
“Recent news reports claiming that 5,000 Bangladeshis have had their visas cancelled in the UAE are inaccurate. According to official data, exactly 626 Bangladeshis have experienced "auto-cancellation" of their visas so far,” she told reporters at a joint briefing with State Minister for Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Md Nurul Haque at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Earlier, they had an inter-ministerial meeting at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Shama Obaed said the situation is not specific to Bangladesh and citizens of other countries, including Nepal, Pakistan, Egypt, and the Philippines, have also faced visa cancellations for various reasons.
“Out of the 626 affected Bangladeshis, details of 417 individuals have already been submitted to the UAE government for visa renewals. Information for the remaining individuals is being processed and forwarded systematically,” she said.
If visas were cancelled due to job termination, the respective employers bear certain responsibilities, said the state minister.
The Bangladeshi Embassy in the UAE is directly coordinating with these companies to find viable solutions, she added.
“We hope we will get a positive result,” said the state minister, encouraging the media to report based on verified facts.
Shama Obaed said expatriates must strictly respect and follow the laws of their host country and refrain from engaging in unlawful activities or posting sensitive or political content on social media platforms. “We want to send out a message - please refrain from engaging in unlawful activities.”
Many migrant workers go abroad after making immense financial sacrifices, and when individuals submit fraudulent or forged documents, it harms the country's reputation and creates hurdles for those attempting to travel legally, she said.
Shama Obaed said the government will consider amendments, if required, to the relevant law to enforce stricter measures against document forgery.
Migration costs from Bangladesh remain significantly higher than those from neighbouring countries like Nepal.
The government has initiated active measures to reduce migration expenses and protect workers from fraudulent middlemen networks.
For the first time in history, Shama Obaed said, a dedicated "Migration and NRB Affairs Wing" has been established within the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to curb illegal migration and human trafficking.

High Aedes risk prompts Tk 50.5C DSCC mosquito budget
item.description:
Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) has allocated Tk50.5 crore for mosquito control insecticides in its Tk4,004.6 crore budget for FY2026-27 after a pre-monsoon survey found Aedes mosquito larval density above the prescribed index in 63 of its 75 wards.
The survey identified 27 wards as high-risk areas, where the corporation carried out special crash programs ahead of the monsoon, according to DSCC Administrator Md Abdus Salam.
Salam unveiled the budget at the DSCC Nagar Bhaban auditorium on Thursday.
The allocation for mosquito control insecticides has increased from Tk45.35 crore in the original FY2025-26 budget. However, the amount was later revised down to Tk30.35 crore.
The FY2026-27 budget also earmarks Tk4 crore for diesel, petrol, oil and lubricants to support mosquito control operations, a category that had no separate allocation in the previous fiscal year's budget.
Another Tk2 crore has been allocated for transportation expenses, including the movement of fogger and wheel spray machines, up from Tk1.5 crore in FY2025-26.
In addition, Tk7.5 crore has been set aside for mosquito control machinery and equipment, compared with Tk2 crore in the revised budget for the previous fiscal year.
In his budget speech, Salam said DSCC had stepped up mosquito control and dengue prevention efforts through regular larviciding in the morning and adulticiding in the afternoon across all wards.
He said mosquito workers and supervisors had received training, while a cross-departmental monitoring team had been formed to ensure mosquito control activities were carried out according to standard procedures.
Salam also said tests conducted by the Ministry of Health found the insecticides currently used by the corporation to be 100% effective. Recommendations from expert teams on alternative insecticides and mosquito control methods were also being implemented regularly, he added.
The administrator said DSCC continued to conduct awareness campaigns through schools and colleges, social media, television commercials, religious institutions and newspaper notices, alongside region-based cleanliness drives involving local public representatives.
"We believe public participation is the greatest tool in preventing dengue," he said.
The Tk4,004.6 crore budget for FY2026-27 was approved at the 14th meeting of the DSCC Governing Committee on July 26.
For FY2025-26, DSCC had originally approved a Tk3,841.38 crore budget, which was later revised to Tk3,138.77 crore.

item.title: Rose Garden: A historic treasure in the heart of Old Dhaka
item.description:
Tucked away amid the bustling streets of Old Dhaka, the historic Rose Garden Palace stands as an enduring symbol of the city's architectural grandeur, aristocratic legacy and political history.
More than a century after its construction, the stately mansion continues to captivate visitors with its elegant design while preserving the stories of a bygone era.
Located on KM Das Lane in Tikatuli, the Rose Garden was once a prestigious residence of Dhaka's elite. Surrounded by lush gardens, ornamental ponds, fountains and intricate decorative elements, the palace remains one of the capital's finest examples of heritage architecture.
A Legacy born in the late 19th century
The Rose Garden traces its origins to the late 19th century, when zamindar(Feudal landlord) Hrishikesh Das commissioned the construction of the palatial residence along with an adjoining rose garden. By the 1930s, the estate had earned widespread recognition for its collection of rose varieties imported from different parts of the world, giving rise to the name "Rose Garden."
Spread across nearly seven acres, the estate was designed to reflect the grandeur of the era. Its imposing central dome, towering Corinthian-style columns, ornate windows, crystal chandeliers and landscaped gardens have made it one of Dhaka's most distinguished historic landmarks.
An architectural masterpiece
The palace showcases a harmonious blend of European architectural influences and local craftsmanship. A spacious forecourt, ornamental pond, sculptures and decorative motifs create an impressive entrance, while stained-glass windows, intricately carved columns and sparkling crystal chandeliers add to its timeless elegance.
In its heyday, the Rose Garden served as a vibrant social and cultural venue, hosting lavish receptions, musical soirées and gatherings of the city's aristocracy.
Preserving a national treasure
Despite changes in ownership over the decades, the Rose Garden has retained its historical and cultural significance.
Recognising its exceptional heritage value, the Department of Archaeology declared the palace a protected monument in 1989. The Government of Bangladesh later acquired the property in 2018, reaffirming its commitment to preserving one of the country's most treasured historic landmarks.
An enduring attraction for visitors
Today, the Rose Garden Palace remains one of Old Dhaka's most cherished heritage attractions. Drawing history enthusiasts, architecture lovers and travellers alike, it offers visitors a rare glimpse into the elegance of the zamindari era and the rich cultural legacy of the old city.
With its seamless blend of history, architecture and political significance, the Rose Garden Palace continues to stand as a living monument to Dhaka's glorious past, preserving memories of a bygone age while inspiring future generations to appreciate and protect the nation's heritage.

item.title: Dengue claims three lives, 467 new cases in 24 hours
item.description:
Health officials on Thursday said they recorded 467 fresh cases of dengue onslaughts killing at least three persons in the past 24 hours.
“During the period, (of the 467) 67 patients were hospitalized in Barisal division, 69 in Chittagong division, 70 in Dhaka division, 57 in Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) and 62 in Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) areas, 66 in Khulna division, 21 in Mymensingh division, 32 in Rajshahi division, 20 in Rangpur division and 3 in Sylhet division, a Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) statement said.
Since the start of the dengue onslaughts, Bangladesh this year witnessed so far 53 deaths while the disease inflicted 15,157.
The dengue last year claimed 413 lives and inflicted 1,02,861 people in the country.
Besides, the dengue claimed 575 lives and inflicted 1,01,214 people in 2024.

item.title: Rizvi stresses rule of law to combat human trafficking
item.description:
BNP Senior Joint Secretary General and Political Adviser to the Prime Minister Ruhul Kabir Rizvi on Thursday underscored the need for stronger anti-human trafficking laws and the effective enforcement of the rule of law, saying trafficking networks flourish where justice is weak.
Addressing a discussion at the RC Majumdar Auditorium of the Theatre Building at the University of Dhaka, Rizvi said human trafficking syndicates are deeply rooted in society and can only be dismantled through impartial law enforcement.
"The government's priority should be to eliminate human trafficking networks, irrespective of their influence or connections," he said.
Emphasising that security is a fundamental right of every citizen, Rizvi warned that poor and lower-middle-income people would continue to fall prey to exploitation and modern-day slavery unless the state ensured legal protection and justice.
He said the lack of the rule of law has fuelled injustice and oppression at the grassroots, where many semi-literate and illiterate people are unable to access local authorities or assert their rights, leaving them particularly vulnerable to exploitation.
He said the state must fulfil its responsibility to protect society, observing that people from developing and Third World countries are among the most frequent victims of human trafficking.
Stressing the need for stronger action, Rizvi said the government must enact tougher anti-human trafficking laws and ensure the effective enforcement of the rule of law to curb the crime.
Rizvi said many people, unaware of the risks, sell their land to brokers and fraudulent agents in the hope of securing jobs abroad, only to become victims of human trafficking.
"After losing everything to trafficking syndicates, many are deported because of legal complications during transit or after reaching their destination. They return home with neither assets nor any means of livelihood," he said.
He said human trafficking is driven by a combination of political and social factors, identifying statelessness, limited economic opportunities and displacement as among its principal causes.
Linking child marriage and inadequate education to the crime, Rizvi said those forced into early marriage often become parents at a young age and are unable to continue their education.
"Without education, they are deprived of opportunities to become self-reliant and improve their lives, making them far more vulnerable to human trafficking," he added.
